text:
mina: RFC follow-up: batch inference pipelines are currently using org keys in CI. propose credential pinning: bind service leases to a specific model pool + project to reduce lateral movement. thoughts? cc @roy @jess

roy: +1. blast radius today is huge. pinning to model pool (gpu-pool-a) + project means a leaked token can't call other projects or pools. but how do we handle model rollovers?

jess: for rollovers, the exchange should support a small grace window and a target whitelist. e.g., allow exchange to request a new lease for the next pool if migration flag present. also audit must show both origin and target pool.

pat: UX: pipelines should register their intent: { repo, pipeline_id, model_pool } once. exchange will only issue leases matching that registration. onboarding should be automated for infra repos.

mina: sketch of issuance API:
```
POST /auth/lease
{ "source_key": "proj-zzz-xxx", "actor": "svc/ci/runner-42", "target_pool": "gpu-pool-a", "ttl": 3600 }
# response: { "lease_token": "lt.s-...", "expires_in": 3600, "bound_to": { "pool": "gpu-pool-a", "project": "infra" } }
```

roy: ops note: enforce mTLS to KMS and mark tokens non-exportable. also add a per-origin quota so a noisy repo can't exhaust pool leases.

jess: security: bind token to both pool-id and file-sig of the pipeline manifest so tokens can't be used by modified clones. we can require the pipeline to present a manifest hash when requesting.

pat: CI change: add a step that attaches the manifest hash to the exchange call. CI runners will store lease in ephemeral credential store and never write it to disk.

audit-bot: rule: all lease issuances must log origin_key_id, actor_id, manifest_hash, target_pool, policy_id. Detected 0 violations in canary. :white_check_mark:

mina: one gap: how do we handle third-party contractors who need infra access across projects? maybe a timebound org-key with scoped capability set, or require contractor services to run from tenant-isolated pool.

roy: prefer tenant-isolated pool for contractors. fewer policy exceptions. org-key should be last-resort emergency only with 2 approvers.

jess: migration plan: 1) feature-flag exchange that enforces pinning, 2) run canary on non-critical customer pipelines, 3) surface list of org-key-using pipelines, 4) auto-suggest registration and manifest pin replacements.

pat: SDK: ExchangeClient.requestLease(manifestHash, pool) helper + credential provider that refreshes leases. warn in logs when a pipeline attempts to request a pool not in its registration.

ci-bot: canary run: exchange v0.1 -> eu-west1, 18 pipelines exercised, 2 failures (manifest hash mismatch). filing ticket #401 for failing pipelines. :gear:

mina: policy question: should tokens be opaque or JWT? for pinned tokens opaque is safer because revocation/cert rotation easier. but gateway might want offline checks. maybe short TTL opaque + gateway cache.

roy: agree opaque + short TTL (5m) with cached introspection at gateway. include minimal origin metadata on introspect response.

jess: follow-up: add a dashboard that shows active leases per pool and top consumers; SOC wants spike alerts. Also include token churn metric.

mina: next actions: I'll write RFC addendum with sequence diagrams and rollback plan. @pat please draft SDK PR and onboarding script. @roy will coordinate ops hardening. Ping audit when ready.

pat: will do, aiming for PR in 2 days. :thumbsup:
